transcript.text: Indesit dryer making a horrible squealing noise when it starts up, goes away after a few mins. Still dries fine

A squeal that’s worst on startup then fades after a few minutes is usually a dry/worn moving part that quietens once it warms up. On an Indesit tumble dryer, common causes are:

• Drum support rollers / rear drum bearing – worn or dry bearings can squeal, then become quieter as they heat up.
• Drive belt or tensioner/idler pulley – a glazed belt or worn pulley bearing often squeals on initial rotation.
• Motor bearings – less common, but can make a high-pitched squeal and eventually worsen.

Because it still dries normally, it may not be an immediate failure, but it generally won’t fix itself and can progress to a seized pulley/bearing, snapped belt, or damaged motor.

What you can safely do:
1. Unplug it first.
2. Clean the lint filter thoroughly and, if it is a condenser/heat-pump model, clean the condenser/filter areas as specified in the manual. Restricted airflow makes components run hotter, though it usually isn’t the direct cause of squealing.
3. Check the drum by hand when empty: it should turn smoothly without roughness, rubbing, or excessive side-to-side movement.
4. Don’t spray WD-40 or oil into the machine — it can contaminate the belt, attract lint, and is not suitable around heat.

Book a repair if the noise persists or gets louder. A technician can identify whether it is the belt tensioner, drum rollers/bearing, or motor. The repair is often worthwhile if the dryer is otherwise in good condition.

Stop using it and unplug it if you notice a burning/rubber smell, scraping or banging, the drum struggles to turn, excessive heat, or the noise becomes constant. Also make sure the filter is cleaned after every load.

If you provide the full model number from the door opening or rear label, I can narrow down the most likely parts and whether that model has a rear bearing/roller arrangement.
Model is IDC8T3B. I've unplugged it and turned the drum by hand, it turns but feels a bit rough with a slight squeak/scrape. Can't tilt it though, bad back.

For an Indesit IDC8T3B, a drum that feels rough and gives a slight squeak/scrape when turned by hand makes a mechanical drum-drive issue much more likely than an airflow/filter issue.

The most likely culprit is the rear drum bearing / drum support shaft, with the belt tensioner pulley and motor bearings also worth checking. The startup squeal that improves after a few minutes is typical of a bearing beginning to dry out or wear.

You do not need to tilt or lift it yourself — especially with a bad back. I’d leave it unplugged and arrange a repair rather than continuing to run it routinely. If the bearing deteriorates it can damage the drum/support, throw or wear through the belt, or eventually cause the drum to bind.

When booking someone, describe it as:

> “Indesit IDC8T3B condenser dryer. Loud squeal on startup which fades after a few minutes; drum feels rough and lightly squeaks/scrapes when turned by hand while unplugged. Please check rear drum bearing/support, belt tensioner/idler and motor bearings.”

Avoid spraying lubricant into it or through the drum: it can contaminate the belt, collect lint, and usually only masks the problem briefly.

If you absolutely need to use it before repair, don’t leave it unattended and stop immediately for a burning smell, hot rubber smell, metal grinding, drum slowing/stopping, or a worsening scrape. But based on the hand-turning roughness, repair sooner rather than later is the sensible option.
